blocks.text: The partition key chooses a group of rows stored together. A clustering column orders rows inside that partition.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_reader(reader_id text,day date,title text,pages int,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id),day)) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY(day DESC);
blocks.title: Design a table for one question

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
Clustering order sorts rows within one Cassandra partition, not across every partition in the cluster.

blocks.text: The table groups a reader's entries by reader_id and orders that reader's days newest first.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This schema allows one row per reader per day. Add another key part if multiple entries per day must be distinct.
